main.claim: Pick a platform, describe yourself in a few lines, choose a tone, and get three bio options you can copy with one click. The options use only the facts you give. Free, no account, 3 runs a day.

sections.heading: How to write your bio
sections.body:
Open the [bio generator](https://bio-generator.lazur.app/) and fill in three things: a platform, a short description of you, and a tone. Then run it and read the three options.

1. Choose the platform: Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter, X, TikTok, Personal website or Dating app.
2. Describe yourself in a few lines. Say what you do, what you care about, and anything else you want people to know.
3. Choose a tone: Professional, Playful, Minimal or Bold.
4. Run it and wait a few seconds for the three options.
5. Copy the option you like and paste it into your profile.

Each run gives you three options, so you can compare them before you pick one.

sections.heading: Pick the platform and the tone
sections.body:
The platform sets the length and style the options aim for. A bio for LinkedIn reads differently from one for TikTok, so choose the platform where you will paste the bio. Use Personal website for a bio on your own site, a speaker page or a newsletter.

The tone sets the voice:

- **Professional** is a measured, formal voice for work profiles.
- **Playful** adds light humor and warmth.
- **Minimal** keeps the bio short and plain.
- **Bold** sounds confident and direct.

If the first run misses, change one thing, such as the tone, and run it again. Changing one input at a time shows you what made the difference.

sections.heading: What the options are built from
sections.body:
The generator writes only from the facts in your description. If you do not mention a job title, a city or a degree, the bio will not add one. That matters for a work profile, where a made-up detail can cause trouble later.

If an option is missing something you want, add that fact to your description and run it again. The options then include it.

Each option is written to fit the length norms of the platform you chose. Check the length in the bio box of that platform before you save, because the box decides what people see.

sections.heading: Copy and paste into your profile
sections.body:
Each option has a copy button, so one click puts it on your clipboard. Open the profile editor on the platform, paste the bio into the bio field, and save.

The steps to find the bio field differ from app to app. If you cannot find it, check that platform's own help page. Answers usually arrive in about 1 to 3 seconds, so you can run a few versions in a minute and keep the best one.

sections.heading: Free use and your text
sections.body:
The generator is free. You get 3 runs a day, and after you leave an email you get 3 more. You do not need an account.

The generator runs on Google Gemini, hosted on Lazur's servers, so the description you type is sent there to write the options. Leave out passwords, bank details and anything you would not share with an online service.

If you write bios, posts and replies every day, Lazur does this in any app on your Mac. Hold two keys, talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

pages.title: Bio Generator for Instagram: 3 Options Free | Lazur
pages.description: Write an Instagram bio in your tone, in three options that fit Instagram's 150-character limit. Built only from facts you give. Free, no sign-up needed.
pages.claim: Choose Instagram, describe your account in a few lines, and pick a tone. You get three bios written to fit Instagram's 150-character limit, using only the facts you gave. Copy one with a click. Free, no account.

sections.heading: Generate an Instagram bio
sections.body:
Open the [Instagram bio generator](https://bio-generator.lazur.app/instagram) and follow these steps.

1. Choose Instagram as the platform.
2. Write two or three lines about your account. Say what you post, who it is for, and one specific fact, such as a city or a hobby.
3. Choose a tone.
4. Run it and compare the three options side by side.
5. Copy the one you like and paste it into your profile.

The more specific your lines, the more specific the options. A line like "I photograph street food in Lisbon" gives the generator something real to work with. A line like "I love life" gives it almost nothing, so the bio will feel generic.

sections.heading: Why the limit is 150 characters
sections.body:
Instagram's Help Center says a bio can be up to 150 characters, and anyone who can see your profile can read it. Plan for every character, including spaces and punctuation, when you check the length.

The generator writes each option to fit the platform you chose. Still, look at the count after you paste. If an option runs over, shorten the last line yourself. Cutting a weak phrase is usually better than cutting the best fact.

sections.heading: Edit your Instagram bio
sections.body:
In the Instagram app, open your profile, tap Edit Profile, and type or paste your text into the bio field. Tap Done to save.

You can also edit on the web. Click your profile icon in the top right, choose Edit Profile, scroll down, and select Submit.

**Hashtags and account links are optional.** In the bio field, type # or @ to see suggestions. The app links the hashtag or account you pick, as Instagram's help pages describe. Add them in the bio field after you paste if you want them.

sections.heading: Choose a tone for your account
sections.body:
The tone should match the account. A personal account can use Playful or Bold, which reads warm and direct. An account for a shop, a studio or a service usually suits Professional, which reads measured and clear. Minimal works for an account where the photos do most of the talking.

Run the generator with two tones and compare the results. Often one tone sounds like you and the other does not. Keep the one that sounds like you, even if it is not the first option.

sections.heading: When the options miss
sections.body:
If none of the three options fits, the description is usually the cause. Add one or two facts you left out, such as what you sell, who you help or what your next post will be about. Then run it again.

The generator uses only facts from your description, so it cannot guess the rest. If an option names something that is not true for you, delete that word before you paste the bio. An option that is short and true beats a long one that is not.

faq.q: How long can an Instagram bio be?
faq.a: An Instagram bio can be up to 150 characters, according to Instagram's Help Center, and anyone who can see your profile can read it. The bio generator writes each option to fit that length, but check the count after you paste, because spaces and punctuation use up characters too.

faq.q: How do I change my Instagram bio?
faq.a: Open your profile in the Instagram app, tap Edit Profile, and type or paste your new text into the bio field. Tap Done to save. You can also change it on the web by choosing Edit Profile from your profile icon and selecting Submit at the bottom of the page.

faq.q: Is the Instagram bio generator free?
faq.a: Yes. You get 3 runs a day, and after you leave an email you get 3 more. You do not need an account to start. Each run gives you three options, and you can copy any of them with one click.

pages.claim: Choose Dating app, describe what you enjoy and what you are looking for, and pick a tone. You get three bio options built only from the facts you gave. Free, no account. Check each app's bio length before you paste.

sections.heading: Write a dating app bio
sections.body:
Open the [dating app bio generator](https://bio-generator.lazur.app/dating-app) and follow these steps.

1. Choose Dating app as the platform.
2. Describe your interests, what you enjoy on a free weekend, and what you are looking for. Two or three lines are enough.
3. Choose a tone.
4. Run it and read all three options out loud.
5. Copy the one that sounds most like you, then paste it into your profile in the app.

Reading out loud helps. A bio that sounds stiff when you say it will look stiff on a screen, so cut or change any line that sounds like a form.

sections.heading: What to put in your description
sections.body:
The generator builds the bio from what you write, so specific details give better options. Good details include a real interest, a place you like to go, a skill, or a kind of conversation you enjoy. A detail like "I bake bread on Sundays and I want someone to try it with me" gives the generator much more to use than "I like fun."

Leave out anything you would not share with a stranger. That means your full name, your home area, your workplace, your school and your phone number. Dating app bios are read by people you have never met, so keep those details out of the description and out of the bio.

sections.heading: Pick a tone that fits you
sections.body:
Playful adds light humor, which suits people who like to start conversations with a joke. Minimal keeps the bio short and plain, which works when your photos say most of the story. Bold sounds direct and sure of itself. Professional is measured and formal, and it is rarely the right choice for a dating profile, but it can help if you want a calm, straightforward tone.

If you cannot choose, run the generator with two tones and compare. Keep the one that sounds like something you would say on a first date.

sections.heading: Check the length in your app
sections.body:
Each dating app sets its own limit for the bio, so the options cannot be checked against one fixed number here. Paste the bio into the app's bio field and look at it there. If the text is cut off or runs too long, shorten the last line yourself.

Cut the weakest line first, not the best fact. A short bio with one clear detail often works better than a long list of interests.

sections.heading: When an option is not right
sections.body:
The generator uses only the facts in your description, so it will not add a job or a hobby you did not mention. If an option says something that is not true for you, delete that part before you paste. If the options feel generic, add a fact that only you would write, then run the generator again.

Saving your favorite option in a note before you paste it lets you compare the next run against it. Keep the version you would be happy to read aloud on a first date.

faq.q: What should I write in my bio for a dating app?
faq.a: Write two or three lines about what you enjoy, what you do for fun, and what you are looking for. Keep it specific, like a band you like or a trip you want to take, and leave out details you would not share with a stranger. The generator builds its options from what you write, so specific input gives more specific bios.

faq.q: How do I write a bio about myself for a dating app?
faq.a: Start with one thing that makes you easy to talk to, then add one or two real interests and a line about what you want. Read it out loud. If it sounds like a form, cut it down. Run the generator to get three drafts in the tone you want, then edit the one that sounds most like you.

faq.q: Does the dating bio generator need an account?
faq.a: No. You can run it without an account. You get 3 runs a day, and after you leave an email you get 3 more. Each run gives you three options, and you can copy any of them with one click. Answers usually arrive in about 1 to 3 seconds.
